title: Replicating the short student videos with a delayed follow-up and a behavioural outcome
rationale: In the source study, Science through the day (about 0.06, SE 0.025) and Science in everyday life (0.063, SE 0.025) were near the threshold among 32 uncorrected tests. The peer-review video had 0.064 (p=0.034). Only immediate trust was measured, so durability and behavioural carry-over are unknown. This confirmatory test concentrates the sample on those three videos plus control and adds a 7-day and a behavioural outcome.
contribution: Provides a Holm-corrected confirmatory test of whether short science videos raise trust, whether any effect lasts 7 days, and whether it changes a behavioural choice.
limitations: Behavioural choice is a hypothetical or low-stakes proxy.
Attrition in the delayed wave may be differential by arm.
Videos differ in content and format, so the design cannot isolate which feature matters.
Online panel sample may not generalise.

design.title: Short student videos: confirmatory test with 7-day follow-up and behavioural choice
design.overview: US adults complete pre-treatment trust items, are randomised to one of three videos or a control page, then report immediate trust and make a behavioural choice. A week later they complete trust again.
design.hypothesis: Each video raises immediate trust relative to control (position a). Under position b, contrasts are near zero after Holm correction. Effects at 7 days are smaller than or equal to immediate effects.
design.primaryOutcome: Immediate post-treatment trust in science (mean of 6 items, items 4-6 reverse-coded), with 7-day trust and the behavioural choice as secondary outcomes.
design.comparison: Each of the three videos against control, with Holm correction across the three contrasts, covariate-adjusted for pre-treatment trust.
design.population: US adults from an online panel such as Lucid, quota-matched to the adult population.

assumptions: Sample about 4000 per arm (16,000 total) to detect 0.03 points at 80% power after Holm correction; the source observed 0.063 (SE 0.025 at n=853-921), and a back-of-envelope estimate gives about 1,000 per arm for 80% power at 0.063. 4,000 per arm gives headroom for effects about half that size and for attrition in the delayed wave.
Equal fixed allocation, no adaptive assignment.
Follow-up sent 7 days after wave 1 with reminders; analysis registered, with Holm correction across three contrasts.
Donation of the $1 bonus is actually paid to a science education organisation.
unresolved: Video files and hosting must be supplied by the research team.
IRB number, compensation and bonus funding are to be set by the research team.
